title: Demo 2 · Agents: one student never speaks
case: Le Yong is on the class list but says nothing. He must get 'no observed participation', never a score of zero.

lines.speaker: Prof Wynter
lines.text: Today is about agents and tool calling. An agent is a loop: the model looks at the conversation, chooses a tool, we run the tool, and we feed the result back in. Let's look at the harness from the lab. What is the observation, the obs variable, after we call run tool?

lines.speaker: Tasmin
lines.text: It's the output of the tool, so the result, or the error message if the call failed.

lines.speaker: Prof Wynter
lines.text: Yes, and why do we return the error to the model instead of crashing?

lines.speaker: Koh Qing Jia
lines.text: So the model can see what went wrong and try again with different arguments.

lines.speaker: Prof Wynter
lines.text: Good. Now, when would you split one agent into several agents with different tools?

lines.speaker: Tina
lines.text: Maybe when the tasks are different, like one agent searches and another one writes, so each prompt stays small.

lines.speaker: Prof Wynter
lines.text: That's one reason. Smaller tool lists also mean fewer wrong tool choices. How would you measure whether an agent is using tools well?

lines.speaker: Tasmin
lines.text: Check if it called the right tool with the right arguments, and how many steps it needed to finish.

lines.speaker: Prof Wynter
lines.text: Tool accuracy and efficiency, good. Alright, for next week read the section on budgets and stopping conditions. Thank you.
